thread:
sophia: heads-up — after last night's BMC firmware roll I see the OOB serial bridge in eu-west-2 start spiking. consoles are multiplexing and sessions are flapping, provisioning stuck on ~18 GPU nodes, CI queues backing up :rotating_light:

james_oncall: acknowledging, looking at the oncall dashboard now. any quick indicators?

sophia: pmacct on the bridge shows lots of tiny packets, TCP retransmits to the management VLAN gateway. noticed MTU mismatch on the serial-bridge host and bmc-bridge which looks new.

tyler_hw: that matches a failed netplan apply during the roll — some hosts reverted to mtu 1500 while the switch expects 9000. can confirm on a node: `ip link show dev oob0` returns `mtu 1500` while config is `9000`.

mina_sre: is this only affecting serial multiplexing or the whole oob plane?

sophia: mostly serial/usb-serial->ipmi tunnels and the console proxy; normal mgmt API traffic seems okay but latency for kexec/provision steps is high.

francesco_infra: noticed BMC websocket sessions accumulating on the proxy. kills pile up and we hit the per-process fd limit. seeing `EMFILE` in the proxy logs.

ops-runbooks: tagging runbook for serial-bridge-mtu. runbook says rollback network change, restart console-proxy, and `systemctl restart oob-bridge`. anyone able to try non-disruptively on a canary rack?

james_oncall: I can run the canary. which rack?

sophia: try eu-west-2-rack7 — it's low-util GPUs. if that clears, we can roll to 4 more racks.

james_oncall: running commands now:
```
ssh op@eu-west-2-rack7-bridge
sudo ip link set dev oob0 mtu 9000
sudo systemctl restart console-proxy
```

james_oncall: applied mtus and restarted proxy. sessions rebounded almost immediately, provisioning resumed for 3 nodes.

mina_sre: good sign. logs show fd count dropping and no more `EMFILE`. can we confirm no other side-effects?

sophia: doing smoke — ping to BMCs OK, `ipmitool chassis status` returns expected on the five tested hosts. one node still stuck in provisioning — looks like kernel panic during kexec recovery earlier, not related to MTU.

tyler_hw: I'll take that stuck node offline for manual inspection. might need serial reattach and NMI dump.

francesco_infra: we should patch the deploy pipeline to assert MTU prev/after in the BMC change job. current rollout didn't validate netplan apply on relay hosts.

ops-runbooks: agree — adding a CanaryStep: `verify_oob_mtu` to the firmware rollout job and a post-check that console-proxy fd usage < 400.

deploy-bot: deployment 2026-03-18T02:10:23Z triggered: bmc-fw-v2.1.4 -> completed (partial rollback to canary applied).

sophia: thanks. two follow-ups: 1) schedule a full rollback window for any rack still showing >3% provisioning failure, 2) add MTU-assert to the preflight checks and alert on fd>500.

james_oncall: noted. I'll open a ticket for automated alerts and assign to infra-pipelines.

kube-capacity: FYI GPU backlog grew ~1100min of queue time during the incident window, cost estimate ~ $2.3k in delayed jobs and retries. tagging billing.

mina_sre: recommend we throttle new provisioning requests to the affected region until the rollout has the MTU check. reduces failure churn.

sophia: agreed — can we set a soft rate limit on the orchestrator for eu-west-2 for next 2 hours?

francesco_infra: done — set `provision_rate_limit: 0.5` for eu-west-2 in the orchestrator.

tyler_hw: note for postmortem — BMC FW change introduced a timing race in netplan apply on relay hosts. need a fix: ensure `ifdown/ifup` sequencing and a follow-up verification `ip link` and `ethtool -k` checks.

ops-runbooks: adding an action item: add verification step + automated revert if MTU mismatch detected.

sophia: filing post-incident doc and tagging owners. thanks everyone for quick triage.

james_oncall: closing loop — rack canary looks stable after 45m, rolling to remaining racks with MTU assertion in place. will update if anything else pops up. :thumbsup:
